facts: Hip tiles displaced onto a flat roof. A storm in Feb 2022 was accepted; no storm around the Apr 2022 date.
decisiveFact: The corner tile loss was storm damage; later slipped tiles fall under accidental damage cover.

facts: Boundary wall failure with gusts around 63 mph recorded.
decisiveFact: The insurer had no photographs to discharge its burden on the gradual-cause exclusion.

facts: Flat roof puddling and sagging decking; a storm in the prior 6 weeks was accepted.
decisiveFact: Decking failure was not consistent with a one-off event; it was gradual.

facts: Ridge tiles with deteriorated mortar; storm confirmed on the date.
decisiveFact: Decline was fair, but 1,100 GBP emergency temporary repair was payable plus 8 percent interest.

facts: Hip tiles; the surveyor photographed a neighbour's roof. 52 mph gust against a 55 mph policy figure was treated as storm.
decisiveFact: The insurer's own images showed mortar cracking and the roofer gave no causation opinion.

facts: Roof valley failure. 50 mph gust against wording requiring 'at least 48 knots'.
decisiveFact: Hard-threshold wording applied; there were poor historical repairs anyway.

facts: Roof leak; the policy contained no storm definition. 32 mph and 4.3 mm/hr recorded.
decisiveFact: The Ombudsman cross-checked named storms and the nearest station and cited Beaufort F9 at 47 mph.

facts: Valley cement failure after flash rain, below the storm definition.
decisiveFact: Two contractors found old cracked cement.

facts: Wall collapse; elderly and disabled policyholders. Wind below threshold.
decisiveFact: Vegetation 'sail effect' was wear and tear; a prompt surveyor visit respected the vulnerability.
A cash-only offer must be at the customer's contractor rates, not the insurer's network rates.

facts: Flat roof and skylight leak; the storm was not disputed.
decisiveFact: There was no visible storm-consistent damage.

facts: Retaining wall failure. 56 mph and 49 mm on one day, 51 mph and 57 mm on another.
decisiveFact: The surveyor relied on Google images and gave inconsistent reasons.

facts: Conservatory flashing. Mean wind 24 mph but gust 67 mph.
decisiveFact: The storm existed (the insurer was wrong on Q1) but the photos showed patch repairs, moss and torn felt.

facts: Roof leak, Nov 2025. Max 25 mph and 11.9 mm/hr.
decisiveFact: Q1 was no; a pixelated screenshot was rejected; internal damage was paid under accidental damage.

facts: Decline on the basis of 'no storm at the stations'; the point was contested.
decisiveFact: The complaint handler's roof-failure theory was not expert evidence.

facts: Wall and fence failure attributed to a 'sail' effect. Gusts of 83 mph.
decisiveFact: The fence exclusion applied; the 25 mm in 24h wording limb was noted.

facts: Wear and tear was defined in the wording.
decisiveFact: Ground-level photography was sufficient on the balance of probabilities.
